https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/16.text: Listen (3 mins) Save Share Ukraine targets Moscow in mass drone attack as Russia bombards Kyiv on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Firefighters work at a Kyiv book market hit by a Russian missile strike on August 16, 2026 [Gleb Garanich/Reuters] By AFP and Reuters Published On 16 Aug 2026 16 Aug 2026 At least one person has been killed and three have been wounded in a Ukrainian drone barrage targeting Moscow, a local official says, as Russia has bombarded Kyiv with ballistic missiles. Russia’s Ministry of Defence said it destroyed 822 drones across the country overnight. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on social media early on Sunday that the city was targeted with 600 drones and “201 drones were destroyed in Moscow region”. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Russia says hit Ukrainian railway and port facilities in new strikes list 2 of 3 Russia stance will be defended in court, pledges World Athletics chief Coe list 3 of 3 Ukraine hits Russian Starlink-style network, Moscow tracks arms package end of list Andrei Vorobyov, governor of the Moscow oblast, wrote on Telegram that an 83-year-old man was killed when a drone hit a private home. At least five people were killed in attacks on southern Russia’s Rostov region, which borders Ukraine, according to regional authorities. The drone assault came after Ukrainian authorities said late on Saturday that at least one person was killed and seven were wounded in Russian air attacks. A woman was killed and six people were wounded in a missile and drone attack on Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in central Ukraine, the region’s governor said. Officials in the capital said Kyiv was “under ballistic missile attack” late on Saturday, with at least one person wounded and fires sparked at nonresidential sites in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi districts. Defence and foreign policy analyst Pavel Felgenhauer told Al Jazeera that the targeting of capital cities suggests an escalation in the war. He noted that Ukraine had managed to bypass air defences in the Moscow region, which has the “best and most dense antiair defences in the entirety of Russia”. The attacks did not hit central Moscow but reached the outskirts of the capital, he added. Advertisement Separately, Romania’s Ministry of National Defence reported on Sunday that a Spanish F-18 jet on a NATO air policing mission to Romania had shot down a drone breaching its airspace. Martin O’Donnell, a spokesman for NATO’s military headquarters, said the alliance is prepared to defend itself. “Additional details regarding Sunday’s incident remain under investigation, but the drone appears to be Russian,” he said. It was the fourth drone shot down in Romania this year . The Defence Ministry wrote on social media that the drone came from neighbouring Moldova. “The surveillance systems of the Ministry of National Defense detected the intrusion of an aerial target into national airspace, coming from the Republic of Moldova,” it said in a statement. Romanian Defence Minister Radu Miruta congratulated the pilots and military personnel on what he called “a successful mission”. In July, a Romanian jet shot down a suspected Russian drone , and in May, a stray drone injured two people in the Romanian city of Galati when it collided with a building. Romania shares a 634km (394-mile) border with Ukraine and has repeatedly seen Russian drones breaching its airspace as Moscow escalates its bombing campaign against Ukrainian civilian and military infrastructure. Escalating long-range strikes Russia has maintained near-daily missile and drone strikes across Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in early 2022, and areas far from the front lines have frequently come under attack. The war’s impact has also spread to key regional shipping routes with reports of mines and unmanned sea drones found floating in the Black Sea. Civilian casualties in Ukraine hit their highest level since 2022 this July, with at least 437 killed and 2,610 injured, according to the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission. Ukraine has increasingly targeted military, industrial and logistical facilities deep inside Russia, arguing its strikes are a response to Moscow’s ongoing bombardment of Ukrainian towns and infrastructure.

https://www.dw.com/en/spain-thousands-pr.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NLhm The rally was a response to the eviction of an 87-year-old woman Image: Susana Vera/REUTERS Advertisement Tens of thousands of people protested in central Madrid on Saturday to denounce Spain 's housing crisis. The demonstrators called for better protection for tenants , anti-fraud rules and a ban on evictions without alternative housing. The march through the center of the Spanish capital was called after an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal , was evicted from her apartment where she had lived for seven decades. Protesters carried signs reading 'we are all Maricarmen' Image: C. Carvajal/JNA/ZUMA/picture alliance The case highlights the growing pressure on long-term tenants in Spain's major cities, where rental prices have surged in recent years. Gentrification and the shortage of affordable housing have fueled public discontent ahead of a general election next year. Analysts say tourism and immigration-driven population growth has put pressure on the already limited housing supply in the cities. The Bank of Spain estimated a shortage of 550,000 homes across the country last year. Toxic tourism — Mallorca's housing crisis To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Protesters camp out in Puerta del Sol Government authorities estimated that around 25,000 people had shown up to protest against Spain's growing housing crisis. The Madrid Tenants' Union, which organized the protest, said over 300,000 had taken part. Once the rally wrapped up, some activists set up a protest camp in the city center's Puerta del Sol square with plans to stay put. Some even pitched up tents to stay the night, or until the police forcibly removed them. Police officers looked on at about a dozen tents, surrounded by thousands of protesters, news agency AFP reported from the scene. Spain previously built homes with public funds that were later sold into private ownership Image: Tomas Calle/JNA Press/Sipa USA/picture alliance Rallying around Abascal The protest was triggered by Maricarmen Abascal's dramatic eviction on Wednesday from the house she had lived in for decades. Abascal was greeted by supporters as she was removed from her home on a stretcher and loaded onto an ambulance. "We're here because housing is a problem that already affects all of society, all ages and classes," said protester Dora Garcia, a 55-year-old nurse. "And we can't keep maintaining this. Housing is a right, and we don't have it," she said. According to Spanish media, Abascal's father first rented the home in the upscale Retiro neighborhood in 1956. After her parents died, she continued to live in the flat, which had a rent cap at the time. Spain: Tourism boom worsens housing crisis To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video In 2018, the building changed ownership, and Urbagestion, an investment fund, bought the unit, raising the rent from €500 ($570) to €2,650 ($3,018). Abascal had been offered an opportunity to buy the apartment before this but could not afford it. The fund later lowered her rent to €1,650, but Abascal could not afford that either. Courts had blocked her eviction three times previously and extensive media coverage turned her into a symbol of the crisis. "This whole housing situation is heartbreaking. Maricarmen has been, in a way, the last straw that sparked this social unrest, but we've been dealing with this whole issue for a long time now," said protester Simón de la Riva, 43, a teacher. "It's unacceptable that vulture funds are buying up homes, that people can't afford to live, that entire families are being evicted, and that an elderly woman has been evicted," she added. https://www.portfolio.hu/global/20261109.text: Elődjéhez hasonlóan a Gerány-5 K5-K is hagyományos aerodinamikai elrendezésű, felsőszárnyas kialakítással, nyilazott szárnyakkal, a farokrészen pedig egyetlen függőleges vezérsíkkal, rögzített vízszintes vezérsíkokkal és oldalkormánnyal rendelkezik. Az alapváltozatnál rövidebb és kisebb fesztávolságú eszköz törzsét a légellenállás csökkentése érdekében alakították át, növelve ezzel a sebességet és a repülési magasságot. A módosításoknak köszönhetően az eszköz maximális repülési magassága ötről hat kilométerre, utazósebessége pedig több mint 450 kilométer/órára nőtt, de egyes manőverek során a végsebessége elérheti az 1000 kilométer/órát is. A drón ezer kilométeres hatótávolsága és a harci részének kilencven kilogrammos tömege nem változott, a hírszerzés által megvizsgált példányba egy TBBCS-90 típusú termobárikus robbanófejet építettek. A fedélzeti elektronika megegyezik a sugárhajtású Gerány-4 Seeker legújabb változataiban használt rendszerekkel. Megtalálható benne a repülésvezérlő, a MOX-modullal ellátott SADRA Seeker inerciális navigációs rendszer, a tizenhat elemes Harxon GI-006 típusú zavarvédett (CRPA) antenna helyben gyártott másolata, valamint egy nyomkövető és egy mesh-modem. A vizsgált példányt felszerelték az új, Szuszanyin nevű elektrooptikai korrelációs rendszerrel is, amelyet a hírszerzés korábban már a Gerany-4-esekben is azonosított. Ez a berendezés a fedélzeti mikroszámítógép memóriájában tárolt referenciaképekkel veti össze az érzékelők által rögzített felvételeket, így biztosítva, hogy a fegyver az indítástól a célpontig pontosan kövesse a kijelölt útvonalat. A K5-K modellben a Szuszanyin rendszer hagyományos optikai szenzorok helyett kétsávos kamerát használ, a képfeldolgozást pedig egy műanyag házba épített Coke Pi mikroszámítógép végzi. Az eszközt egy TRD-200 típusú gázturbinás sugárhajtómű hajtja, amelyet kínai alkatrészekből szerelnek össze az alabugai üzemben. A fegyverben azonosított kilencvenhárom elektronikai részegység legnagyobb része amerikai, kínai és svájci gyártóktól származik. A műszaki jellemzőktől, az üzemanyag-kapacitástól és a fedélzeti felszereltségtől függő hatótávolságú orosz sugárhajtású drónok Ukrajna nyugati régióit is képesek elérni. Az ukrán légvédelem azonban egyre hatékonyabban lép fel ezekkel az eszközökkel szemben, a Gerany-4 típusú drónok esetében az elfogási arány jelenleg megközelíti a hatvan százalékot.
